response.reasoning: Both accounts here can be true at once, and I think they largely are. The record of the purchase shows the parcel travelled and was delivered on 28 August, and the buyer said something was wrong the same day it arrived — so there is no gap in time that would make me doubt the damage was there on opening. The buyer asked specifically about box condition before paying and was told the boxes were fine, and the listing itself promised "boxes in good condition", so box condition is fairly treated as part of what was paid for. On the other hand, the buyer's own photograph of the outer shipping carton shows a crushed and split corner on the carton itself, in the same area as the crushing visible on the set box. That points to damage happening in transit rather than the seller sending a box that was already crushed, which is consistent with the seller's statement that it left in good condition. It also shows the set travelled in a single carton with little apparent protection at the corners, which is the seller's side of the shipping to arrange. What actually arrived is not worthless: the photograph of the set box shows one crushed and rubbed corner with some edge wear, on a box that is otherwise whole and presentable, and only one of the four sets is affected. Nothing suggests the contents of any set are missing or damaged. So the shortfall against what was described is a real but partial loss of value on roughly a quarter of the purchase, with the seller carrying the risk of how it was packed for the journey. A quarter of the money being held to the buyer reflects that loss without treating a delivered, mostly intact group of four sets as a failed purchase.

findings.statement: The parcel was delivered on 28 August 2026 and the buyer reported the damaged box the same day, so there is no unexplained delay between arrival and the complaint.
Before buying, the buyer asked specifically about box condition and was told the boxes were fine; the listing also described the boxes as in good condition at a price of 200 for four sets.

The buyer's photograph of the outer shipping carton shows a crushed, split corner on the carton itself, in the same region as the damage to the set box, which points to the harm occurring during the journey rather than before it was sent.

The set box shown is crushed and rubbed at one corner but otherwise complete and intact, and only one of the four sets is said to be affected, with no indication that any contents are missing or damaged.
The seller states the item was in good condition and carefully packed; the photograph of the carton shows a single box with damage concentrated at an unprotected corner.
